questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The nature (mountains, the lake), conservative and nice city, law institutions like WTO and UN.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Lots of new friends, new cultures and great little trips to France.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was not that easy, but doable.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A lot, there was both it-workers and a good information-day, where every question was answered.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There was studio apartments, and dorm rooms. I recommend choosing the studio appartements. The higher price is worth it, and the dorm rooms are far from nice.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Cooking facilities was limited since we very 16 people using the same small kitchen with only 1 stove.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend choosing a studio apartment, but it was very nice to live with people who are also studying at UNIGE. You can study together and relate to the same circumstances. But the surroundings and the environment was not the best. There were holes in the wall, stains and black mold. 
There were other housings available to students, and Cité Universitaire is not recommended.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Good neighbors, kind students, nice vibe. Bad housing.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was okay.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Sending a lot of information and documents.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not a lot. Arnoud was our council, and he was sometimes not the fastest. But to be fair, he has a lot of students to answer.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very. I got into all my classes.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: To stay patient, everything will work out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Great teachers, but poor acces to knowledge of the exam, and the exam was very informal.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses was not that high. I believe the level on Copenhagen University is higher.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very different. But it was also good. The teachers were very committed and passionate.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Comparative Human Rights, Comparative Contract Law, European Competition Law, International Arbitration, Law of Trust.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Competition Law was very interesting and a bit more challenging than the other subjects. Arbtitration Law was easy to follow if you were not in the mood for a challenge. Law of trust is interesting, also a bit challenging and a nice oral exam with a good Professor.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: More expensive to live in Geneva than I expected. Grocery shopping is expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Nothing was less expensive than expected. Everything was more expensive than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A lot of sport opportunities. And even if I did not party, there was a lot of oppertunities to do so.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything from Pilates to Volleyball and a gym.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend joining the Hiking Club and also to join the Gym at Cité. It is very inexpensive and it has the basic gear to strength train.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: It was amazing in Annecy (the Venice of the Alps) and Chamonix (for skiing). Otherwise hiking up Mont Saléve near by (with a cafe on top) or Stoos Ridge (also in Switzerland).

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. A calm and conservative Culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I was mostly with other danish students. Otherwise I would join the sport activities like dance or some vulenteer work to get to know the others.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There was not any cultural differences that was challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I appreciated that the people were clean, polite and did not throw trash. I Appreciated that the city held a lot of co-students, elder people and families. It is a city good for working and studying.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Do not postpone your readings to the exam, do them during and then you might not have to study as hard in the exam period. Since the subjects have such little credits (6 ECTS) you will end up having to do 5 exams. 
Take as many small trips outside Geneve as you can. More Hikes in Switzerland or visit Italy. 
Grocery shop in Lidl or use Too good to go, then you can save some money.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No, Law was not to demanding, and we had a lot of time for other things. Some of the other faculties, barely leaves any time for anything other than school.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: That I got so many new danish friends. And that I learned a lot about completely different cultures. In my residence there was everything from Mexican to Russian and Japanese. I heard all about their home cities, cultures and opinions. Very exciting.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was just being away from home or to manage some of the practical errands. Like residence permit or insurance. But it was not that challenging.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
